It is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and GDPR compliant. Lavender is backed by Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: Zenput
providers.description: Zenput (now Crunchtime Ops Execution) is an operations-execution platform for multi-unit restaurant and convenience-store operators, used across 60,000+ locations in 100+ countries to run task management, audits and food-safety compliance, temperature monitoring, food-prep labeling, and store-level operational workflows. Zenput exposes a RESTful HTTP API (documented at developer.zenput.com) for submissions/form data, locations, users and roles, teams, tasks, sensors, calendar events / operating hours, general attributes, and field-business-consultant (FBC) assignments. The API authenticates with a per-user X-API-TOKEN header, is versioned in the URL path (v1 and v3), and provides a large-batch submissions retrieval flow with token-based paging plus a staging environment for testing. Zenput was acquired by Crunchtime in 2022 and continues to operate its developer platform under the Zenput brand.

providers.name: Athena
providers.description: Athena is an executive assistant service that pairs entrepreneurs, founders, and executives with dedicated, full-time remote executive assistants, along with the recruiting, training, and delegation coaching needed to work with them effectively. Athena screens a large global applicant pool and accepts only a small fraction, then equips its assistants with proprietary in-house AI tooling to maximize productivity across email, scheduling, research, travel, and day-to-day operations. The company is headquartered in San Juan, Puerto Rico and is backed by investors including Khosla Ventures. Athena is a services company with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Monograph
providers.description: Monograph is firm-management software purpose-built for architecture and engineering (A&E) practices, unifying project management, resourcing and staffing, time tracking, budgeting, invoicing and client payments in one connected system. Used by thousands of US-based A&E firms, it integrates with QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, but publishes no public developer API, webhooks, or SDKs. Backed by Homebrew and Index Ventures.

providers.name: Ventrilo.ai
providers.description: Ventrilo.ai is a San Francisco AI startup (founded 2023, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Bloomberg Beta, Conviction, Rain Capital, 112 Capital, and Gil Capital) building an AI browser assistant delivered as a Chrome extension. The product connects your open tabs, remembers context, auto-fills forms, drafts and rewrites text in place, and answers questions grounded in the pages you are working in — "no copy-pasting, no starting over." It ships as a free tier plus a $20/month Plus plan via chat.ventrilo.ai. The company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; its api.ventrilo.ai backend is private (HTTP 401). It does publish an RFC 9116 security.txt, a responsible-disclosure security policy with safe harbor, and claims SOC 2 certification. Not related to the classic Ventrilo VoIP software.

providers.name: Ctrl
providers.description: Ctrl (Ctrl, Inc., a Delaware corporation) is an AI-powered workspace for revenue and sales teams that consolidates the tools and data a rep needs — CRM, email, calendar, and messaging — into a single actionable view. Founded in 2021 by Omri Sagzan and Aviv Nahum and based in Tel Aviv and London, Ctrl automates the manual work of updating records across apps such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Workspace, and Slack, and helps teams codify and replicate their winning sales playbooks. The company raised a $9M seed round led by LocalGlobe and Earlybird in 2023 and was acquired by Sana Labs in October 2024. Ctrl is a UI/workspace product surfaced as an Earlybird portfolio company; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Supafax
providers.description: Supafax is an AI email assistant and autonomous inbox agent from Veriad, Inc. (Y Combinator Winter 2026) that lives inside Gmail and Outlook to proactively manage email and calendar. It drafts context-aware replies in your writing style, auto-labels and prioritizes messages, schedules and books meetings through back-and-forth coordination, answers inbox queries, and runs custom automation rules defined in plain English. Founded in 2025 in San Francisco by Rohan Mahendraker and Anton Muratov, Supafax sells a Professional plan and an Enterprise tier with SSO/SCIM, custom integrations, and dedicated support. It is a consumer/B2B productivity product with no public developer API at this time; its security posture (security.txt, CASA Tier 2, ICO registration, GDPR) is its most developer-relevant public surface.

providers.name: Almanac Leie1
providers.description: Almanac Labs, Inc. (almanac.io) is a San Francisco-based productivity company building an async collaboration platform positioned as "the fastest wiki and workflow tool ever built." Almanac consolidates a team's documents into an organized single source of truth, pairing a modern doc editor with version control, structured review/approval workflows, and reusable templates. Founded in 2017 and backed by General Catalyst, the company also ships the Almanac API (V1, private beta) for programmatic workspace management — importing files, moving files and folders, listing workspace users and groups, reading and updating document properties and access, and managing document and folder metadata. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio lead and enriched from Almanac's public marketing, developer help, changelog, and legal pages.

providers.name: Genspark
providers.description: Genspark is an all-in-one AI workspace and autonomous "Super Agent" platform that plans and executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf. It bundles a suite of AI agent tools — deep research, AI slides, AI sheets, AI docs, AI chat, a "Call For Me" voice agent, and a built-in AI browser — into a single natural-language workspace, alongside companion products such as Genspark Claw, Speakly, GenClipboard, and GenTerminal and native iOS and Android apps. For developers and agents, Genspark operates a hosted, remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at /api/mcp that exposes its tools, resources, and prompts over HTTP, gated by OAuth 2.1 (authorization_code with PKCE, refresh tokens, and dynamic client registration). Genspark is backed by Emergence Capital.

providers.name: Sudowrite
providers.description: Sudowrite is an AI writing platform built specifically for fiction and creative writers, used by 300,000+ authors from debut novelists to bestselling professionals. Its fiction-trained Muse AI model, alongside Story Bible (AI-powered character, worldbuilding, plot, and style memory), First Draft chapter drafting, and tools like Write, Rewrite, Describe, Expand, Brainstorm, and Canvas, helps writers draft, revise, and develop stories faster without sacrificing their voice. Sudowrite also offers a 1,000+ plugin marketplace, multi-model support (Sudowrite Muse, Claude, GPT, Gemini), and web plus iOS/Android apps. Named "a salvation" by The New Yorker and featured in The New York Times, The Verge, Time, and Wired. Sudowrite publishes no public developer API; the surface here is its consumer product, docs, and support properties.

providers.name: JobNimbus
providers.description: JobNimbus is a CRM and project management platform built for contractors, particularly in roofing, restoration, and home services industries. The platform enables lead tracking, job scheduling, estimating, invoicing, document management, and workflow automation. JobNimbus exposes a REST-like Open API supporting GET, PUT, and POST requests with JSON payloads, authenticated via API keys generated from the user dashboard.

providers.name: Osly
providers.description: Osly is an AI workflow automation platform (a product of Alore AI) that lets startups and prosumers build N8N-based AI workflows from natural language, with no coding required. Users describe automations in plain English to generate email sequences, lead categorization and personalized outreach, spin up internal dashboard UIs, and connect 50+ apps including HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Drive, Notion, LinkedIn and Shopify. Osly was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no OpenAPI; the only machine-readable description of its API is the company's own first-party TypeScript SDK in github.com/Osly-AI, which documents an X-API-Key REST surface plus a Socket.IO execution stream at api.pocketflow.ai — the company's prior brand domain, since pocketflow.ai redirects to osly.ai. As of 2026-08-14 every application and API host in the estate (app.osly.ai, api.osly.ai, api.pocketflow.ai, app.alore.ai) returns Cloudflare 522; only the marketing site and blog respond.

providers.name: Delightree
providers.description: Delightree is an AI-powered franchise operations platform that consolidates franchise management into a single operating system for headquarters and location teams. It combines a centralized knowledge base, interactive training, task management, forms and checklists, audits, a location launcher for opening new stores, team communication, and reporting so franchisors can standardize and enforce standard operating procedures across every location. The platform is built around frontline franchisee adoption and serves 150+ franchise brands across food and beverage, fitness, wellness, home services, and other multi-unit, regulated sectors. Backed by Accel; profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or documentation program was found during enrichment (2026-07-18).

providers.name: HyperWrite
providers.description: HyperWrite (by OthersideAI) is an AI writing assistant plus Personal Assistant and Agent product line that combines AutoWrite, TypeAhead, HyperChat, an AI Document Editor, Scholar AI research, and a Chrome extension that lets an agent take real actions in the browser (Gmail, LinkedIn, shopping, travel). HyperWrite has historically described a partner/API program for its agent, but there is no fully public self-serve API reference - profiled here through the consumer product surface.

providers.name: Quip
providers.description: Quip is a Salesforce-owned collaborative productivity platform that combines documents, spreadsheets, chat, and tasks into a single workspace tightly integrated with the Salesforce CRM. It enables teams to embed live data, collaborate in real time, and automate workflows across deal collaboration, account planning, and sales operations. The Quip Automation API is a REST interface for creating and managing threads, documents, messages, folders, and users with OAuth 2.0 Bearer token authentication.

providers.name: ConstructionOnline
providers.description: ConstructionOnline is UDA Technologies' cloud construction project management platform covering estimating, scheduling, budgets, change orders, daily logs, file sharing, and client and subcontractor collaboration. UDA exposes the platform through a documented REST API available to ConstructionOnline Business and Enterprise customers, with read and write access for projects, contacts, schedules, and financials. Access is gated by an application process (api@uda1.com), authenticated with company-issued credentials, and rate-limited to 500 requests per hour per account.

providers.name: Pitch
providers.description: Pitch is a collaborative presentation software company (pitch.com) that builds a fast, web-based tool for teams to create, share, and present decks together in real time, with templates, brand controls, live collaboration, analytics, and in-product integrations. Backed by Index Ventures and tracked in the API Evangelist network. As of this profile Pitch publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or MCP server; enrichment here captured its published security and identity surface.

providers.name: Volt
providers.description: Volt is a desktop application (Mac, Windows, and Chrome) that supercharges WhatsApp for professionals and sales teams — turning long voice notes into readable transcripts and summaries, scheduling messages, adding keyboard-first navigation, organizing chats into focused workspaces, and sending personalized broadcasts. Message content stays under WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption and never passes through Volt's own servers. For agents and AI models, Volt runs an authenticated remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes WhatsApp contacts, chats, messages, groups, and lists as tools. Volt is backed by 500 Global, EQT Ventures, and IVP.

providers.name: SmartSuite
providers.description: SmartSuite is a collaborative work management platform that helps teams plan, track, and manage workflows, projects, and everyday tasks using customizable solutions, tables, records, and automations. The platform combines spreadsheet, database, project management, and workflow automation capabilities into a unified workspace. SmartSuite's REST API provides programmatic access to Solutions, Tables, Records, and Fields using token-based authentication.

providers.name: Ellipsus
providers.description: Ellipsus is a collaborative writing platform built for creative and fiction writers, combining a modern text editor with granular, Git-style version control so authors can draft, branch, share, and merge work together across devices. Founded in 2022 and operated by a small distributed team across Berlin (Germany), Madrid (Spain), and Szczecin (Poland), the product threads collaboration through every stage of writing — organizing drafts, discussing feedback, tracking changes, and preserving public version history — with a writers-first, artist-ownership, anti-AI-generated-content stance. Ellipsus offers a free tier and a paid Plus license, and is backed by Speedinvest. It is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Cron
providers.description: Cron was a next-generation calendar application for professionals and teams, backed by Initialized Capital and later acquired by Notion, where it was rebranded and relaunched as Notion Calendar. The product offered a fast, keyboard-driven desktop and mobile calendar with multi-account scheduling, time-zone handling, team availability, and deep Notion workspace integration (calendar events linked to Notion pages and databases). Cron is an end-user consumer product and does not expose a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site, a dated changelog (retired January 2024 at the Notion Calendar rebrand), a blog, and help documentation now hosted within Notion. This profile captures Cron's public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Almanac Labs
providers.description: Almanac Labs, Inc. builds Almanac, an enterprise wiki and async collaboration platform that consolidates a team's scattered documents into a single, organized source of truth. Almanac combines fast document editing, wikis, version control, approvals, and workflow/task management to replace tools like Confluence, Notion, and Asana, and it publishes company handbooks and community-powered documentation. The Almanac API (V1, private beta) lets workspaces import and move files and folders, view users and groups, read and update document properties, manage who has access to documents, and access and update metadata for documents and folders. Almanac integrates with Slack, Figma, Loom, and GitHub, and is backed by General Catalyst. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Almanac's public surface.

providers.name: TransparentBusiness
providers.description: TransparentBusiness is a New York based SaaS company, founded in 2012 by Alex Konanykhin and Silvina Moschini, that sells a cloud platform for managing and monitoring remote workforces: a desktop timer, screenshot-based activity verification, timesheets, task assignment, and real-time project cost and progress reporting for distributed teams and contractors. The company also operates the SheWorks! and Yandiki talent marketplaces and the CloudWorking Academy training platform, and was later renamed Unicoin, Inc. The product is delivered as a hosted web application plus downloadable desktop timer clients; the company publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Spike
providers.description: Spike is an AI-powered email and team collaboration platform that turns standard email accounts (Gmail, Outlook, IMAP) into a chat-like, conversational experience. Its consumer Email App reformats existing inboxes into threaded conversations, while Spike Teamspace is an end-to-end email and team-chat service with shared inboxes, channels, groups, collaborative docs, tasks, notes, and built-in video meetings. Spike layers AI features across the inbox for smart prioritization, thread summaries, and draft assistance. The company is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass Spike ships consumer and team applications but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; the profile below captures its real product, security posture, and public link surface.

providers.name: Immersed
providers.description: Immersed is a spatial-computing company that turns AR/VR headsets into portable multi-monitor workspaces for remote work, coding, and collaboration. Its free desktop agent streams up to five virtual screens into headsets such as Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, GalaxyXR, and Pico, adding solo focus environments plus multi-user telepresence with screen sharing and whiteboarding. Immersed is also building Visor, its own lightweight 4K-per-eye standalone headset. The company is Techstars-backed. Immersed publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, product, security, and llms.txt surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Buildforever
providers.description: BuildForever is a consumer software company building products that feel personal, magical, and deeply human. Its first product, Extra (extra.email), is a free AI email app for iPhone, Mac, and Gmail that automatically organizes the inbox into smart categories, summarizes what matters in a daily digest, cleans up subscriptions and unwanted senders, answers natural-language questions about your mail, and drafts replies in your own tone. Founded and led by CEO Naveen Gavini (formerly SVP/CPO at Pinterest), BuildForever is backed by Abstract Ventures, Felicis, and DST Global, with angel investors including Ben Silbermann, Guillermo Rauch, and Paul Buchheit. The company does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its consumer product surface and identity.

providers.name: Dework
providers.description: Dework is a Web3-native task-management and bounty platform for DAOs and decentralized teams. Organizations create bounties, projects, and task boards; contributors build an on-chain reputation profile, claim or apply to tasks, and get paid in the DAO's own token or stablecoins from supported wallets (Gnosis/Safe, MetaMask, Phantom, WalletConnect). Dework offers token- and Discord-role gating, two-way Discord and GitHub sync, Notion and Coordinape integrations, batch payments, reputation staking, roadmaps, and leaderboards. It aggregates bounties and grants from hundreds of DAOs. The app is backed by an Apollo GraphQL API at api.dework.xyz; product documentation lives on GitBook. Backed by Paradigm.

providers.name: Northspyre
providers.description: Northspyre is a real estate development management platform that gives owners, developers, and project teams an end-to-end system for managing deals, projects, and portfolios across the full development lifecycle — acquisition, early planning, pre-development, construction, and stabilization. It unifies siloed project data and automates routine work with tools for financial modeling and deal pipeline management, budget and cost control, vendor procurement and management, forecasting, portfolio analytics, and investor and lender reporting. Northspyre is delivered as a hosted SaaS application and is SOC 2 Type II certified. It exposes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity, compliance posture, and domain security.

providers.name: Lisan
providers.description: Lisan is an AI-powered Arabic proofreading and writing-assistance platform, headquartered in the UAE and backed by 500 Global. Its language engine detects and corrects eight classes of error in Arabic text — spelling, grammar, morphology, semantics, style, formatting, proper nouns, and citations — and returns context-aware suggestions together with explanations that help writers build language skill, plus error statistics and performance reporting. Lisan reaches writers through a web application, a Windows desktop app, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint and Outlook add-ins, Chrome and Edge browser extensions, and a WordPress plugin. For institutions it adds enforcement of an organization's own style guide, writing-productivity tooling, and analytics dashboards, and it advertises an API and SDK for developers. As of July 2026 that developer surface is not publicly documented — Lisan publishes no developer portal, API reference, base URL, or machine-readable specification, and API/SDK access is arranged through its institutional contact channel.

providers.name: Beep
providers.description: Beep (Just Beep It!) is a visual feedback and web collaboration platform that helps teams review live websites, report bugs, run user testing, and collect ideas directly on the page. Delivered primarily as a browser extension, it lets users annotate any web page, leave comments, attach files, and record their screen so feedback moves faster and projects ship sooner. The product targets agencies, product teams, and builders, offers a free tier plus a paid SuperBeeper plan and enterprise pricing, and is built on Wix. It exposes no bespoke developer REST API, but its Wix-powered site publishes an llms.txt and a public Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic AI access. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Handoff
providers.description: Handoff is an AI-native construction management and estimating platform built for residential contractors — remodelers, home builders, handymen, and trade contractors. It handles estimating, AI takeoffs, proposals, project management, scheduling, CRM, change orders, invoicing, and financial management end-to-end, generating detailed, localized estimates in seconds from descriptions, photos, drawings, or voice. Built by 1build and backed by Initialized Capital, Greycroft, Y Combinator, and Masco Ventures, Handoff serves 10,000+ monthly active users managing billions in annualized residential construction projects. Handoff does not currently expose a public developer API; it offers a Zapier integration for connected workflows, with an API on its public roadmap.

providers.name: Jellyfish
providers.description: Jellyfish is a software engineering intelligence (SEI) platform that turns data from developer tools — issue trackers (Jira, Linear, Azure Boards), source control and CI/CD (GitHub, Azure DevOps), and AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Amazon Q, Gemini Code Assist) — into productivity and business-impact insights for R&D leaders. The platform measures AI adoption, engineering allocation, and delivery across the software development lifecycle through a Data Hub, extensible dashboards, and AI-assisted custom queries. Jellyfish is an enterprise, demo-gated product with no public self-service API; data access is delivered through the product and its integrations rather than a documented developer API. Backed by Accel, Insight Partners, and Wing Venture Capital.

providers.name: Blomma
providers.description: Blomma is an AI-powered career coaching platform that pairs artificial intelligence with emotional intelligence to act as a private thinking partner for professionals. Through chat-based coaching, guided reflection, goal-setting with built-in accountability, a personal journal, and a growth dashboard, Blomma helps founders, people leaders, and ambitious professionals turn abstract aspirations into concrete, trackable goals, and can personalize coaching from uploaded performance reviews and development plans. It is delivered as a consumer subscription through web and mobile apps, with custom team plans for organizations, and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Thorin
providers.description: Thorin is an applied-AI startup incubated and backed by 8VC (Joe Lonsdale), building a workbench for company agents. Its product at app.thorin.com pairs a personal agent that acts as your delegate with project agents that own shared team workflows, connecting business systems (Slack, Google Workspace, Notion, Gong, Salesforce, Affinity, and MCP) and organizing company context into feeds that power reusable skills and scheduled automations. Thorin observes work across email, chat, meetings, and documents to build a real-time model of how a business operates, then automates recurring processes such as deal flow, deal-prep briefs, and inbox switchboards. Seed-stage, based in San Francisco. This profile documents Thorin's product and documentation surface; no public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Granthika
providers.description: Granthika is a writing-software company founded by novelist Vikram Chandra (author of Sacred Games) and Borislav Iordanov. Its product is a first-of-its-kind semantic editor for professional and aspiring writers that lets authors capture and manage the knowledge inside a manuscript — characters, locations, events, and narrative structure — as they write, then integrate that knowledge back into the text. Features include universe/knowledge building, a timeline, semantic search, an intelligent analyzer, and language assistance, delivered as both an online app and a desktop application with free trials and educational subscriptions. Granthika was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. It publishes no bespoke developer/product API; its marketing site runs on Wix, which exposes a public Wix Site MCP endpoint and an llms.txt for agentic access to public site content.

providers.name: Graneet
providers.description: Graneet is a French vertical-SaaS ERP for the construction and public-works (BTP) sector, built for small and mid-sized contractors (roughly EUR 2M to 100M in revenue) to protect project profitability from the office to the job site. It unifies cost estimating and quotations, progress (situation) invoicing, purchase and supplier-invoice management, project planning and labor tracking, cash and bank reconciliation, and real-time margin dashboards, with a companion mobile app and prebuilt integrations to accounting tools such as Sage 100 and Pennylane. The product is delivered as a cloud application (app.graneet.com) backed by internal Main, BFF, and Quotation APIs; there is no public developer API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Switchyards
providers.description: Switchyards is a membership-based neighborhood work club — a 24/7 network of coffee-shop-style workspaces built for focused solo work close to where members live. Each club pairs a bustling cafe with quiet library spaces for deep work, plus bookable phone booths and meeting rooms, free locally roasted coffee and organic tea, and fast internet. Membership runs about $100/month for unlimited access across all locations, and the company is expanding from its Atlanta roots into neighborhoods across the Southeast and beyond. Switchyards is backed by Bullpen Capital and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Balloon
providers.description: Balloon is a research-backed team collaboration and decision-making platform built to eliminate groupthink and give quieter voices a psychologically safe way to contribute. Its core workflow, called a "flight," is a two-stage, partly anonymous process in which a leader poses a question, team members submit ideas ("balloons") and discuss them, and the group then evaluates and "pumps" the strongest ideas on merit, surfacing a Balloon Score that shows consensus and buy-in. Balloon ships 150+ expert-authored flight templates across 25 business areas and supports asynchronous, time-zone-independent participation, positioning itself as a replacement for status and ideation meetings (the company cites a 70% reduction in meeting time and that ~80% of information shared is new to the organization). Founded by Amanda Greenberg and Noah Bornstein, Balloon is backed by 500 Global and other investors, with an advisory board including Adam Grant, Amy Edmondson, and Daniel Pink. It is a SaaS web application (app at balloon.app) with no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: IKI AI
providers.description: IKI AI is an AI-native workspace for knowledge, research, strategy, and creative work, backed by 500 Global. It pairs an AI assistant that summarizes, highlights, and connects saved content with an AI editor that grounds writing in a user's personal knowledge base, plus shared Team Spaces and a browser extension for one-click webpage saving with notes. The product targets researchers, students, consultants, copywriters, coaches, lawyers, founders, and venture teams, and emphasizes privacy with a choice of top-tier LLMs. IKI AI is delivered as a consumer and team SaaS (web app at app.iki.ai and a Chrome extension) with subscription plans; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI. This profile tracks its public identity, commercial, and security surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Paperplane
providers.description: Paperplane is an AI sales-productivity tool (Y Combinator W23, backed by Bloomberg Beta) that automatically takes notes on sales calls and keeps a rep's CRM up to date. It connects to a team's calendar and to conversational intelligence and call-recording tools such as Gong and Chorus, transcribes and analyzes each call, then writes the results back to Salesforce — updating opportunity fields, notes, and action items so sales teams spend less time on manual CRM data entry and stay on top of their deals. The product is organized around opportunities, calls, and notes, with integrations for Google Calendar, Gong, Chorus, and Salesforce. Paperplane appears to have wound down: Y Combinator lists the company as Inactive (and now describes it as a credit risk management platform for builders' merchants, so it pivoted at least once before stopping), its marketing site presents no TLS certificate, its application host returns a Vercel 402 DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED, and its API host is an Envoy ingress that 404s every path with an empty body. Two surfaces remain live: a GitBook documentation site — which is an unfilled starter template carrying GitBook's own placeholder copy, last updated three years ago — with an llms.txt index, and a Clerk-hosted OpenID Connect identity instance at clerk.paperplane.ai that still serves real OIDC and RFC 8414 discovery documents. There is no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, MCP server, or agent card.

providers.name: Thomson Reuters
providers.description: Thomson Reuters provides over 137 APIs across legal, tax and accounting, risk and fraud, and trade and supply industries through their global developer portal. APIs cover Westlaw legal research, Checkpoint tax content, ONESOURCE tax software, HighQ document management, Legal Tracker matter management, and risk and fraud solutions including identity verification and adverse media screening.

providers.name: Gartner
providers.description: Gartner, Inc. (NYSE IT) is a global research and advisory firm selling syndicated research, analyst inquiry, benchmarking, peer communities and conferences to executives across IT, finance, HR, supply chain, marketing, sales, legal and customer service. Gartner publishes no public developer API, developer portal or machine-readable contract: the research library and the Peer Insights vendor portal are subscription-gated, and the one live first-party API host found by probe (gapi.gartner.com, an AWS API Gateway) rejects every anonymous request. Gartner sold its Digital Markets business - Capterra, GetApp and Software Advice, and the Buyer Discovery API that serves their intent data - to G2 in February 2026, so the only OpenAPI reachable on a gartner.com host belongs to G2. This repository tracks the company and any first-party technical artifact that surfaces over time.

providers.name: Planera
providers.description: Planera is a modern construction scheduling platform for builders and general contractors, purpose-built around the Critical Path Method (CPM). It lets teams build, manage, and optimize project schedules through a visual, collaborative interface with drag-and-drop editing, a digital whiteboard (Canvas), Gantt views, DCMA quality checks, resource planning, and an AI scheduling assistant (Manny) for scenario analysis and risk identification. Planera spans pursuits, preconstruction, operations, and enterprise portfolio management, offers an iPad field app, and integrates with Procore, Autodesk, Primavera P6, and Microsoft Project. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 certified and is backed by Sierra Ventures.

providers.name: Cabinet
providers.description: Cabinet is a calendar management and scheduling automation platform built for executive assistants and the leaders they support. It brings group scheduling polls, copy-and-paste availability, unique booking links, shadow holds, and a shared meeting log into one all-in-one workspace, and integrates with Outlook and Google Calendar plus Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. Trusted by over 2,000 companies, Cabinet is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant and continuously monitored by Secureframe. It was founded by former executive assistant Julia Leibowitz and is backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Locale
providers.description: Locale is a no-code workflow automation platform that lets operations, data, and engineering teams build, run, and monitor automated workflows without writing glue code. Its visual builder chains together apps and actions — HTTP requests, AI Actions, run-your-own code, email, Slack, PostgreSQL, Sendgrid, and Fireflies.ai — with flow controls such as conditional branching, delays, and list iterators, then passes data between steps to orchestrate real business processes. Workflows can be built, connected, debugged, and published from the Locale app, and the platform positions itself as an operational automation layer for teams that want internal alerting and process automation without a heavy engineering lift. Locale is backed by a16z. This profile was enriched from Locale's public documentation surface (docs.locale.ai); Locale publishes no first-party public REST API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Venue
providers.description: Venue is an all-in-one internal communications platform that makes it easy for teams to host, organize, and share all hands, webinars, AMAs, and fireside chats. It combines HD live streaming, recording, automatic transcription and summarization, branded Q&A, engagement tracking, and Channels for centralizing events and videos. Aimed at internal comms and employer-brand teams at companies like Shopify, PwC, Wealthsimple, and Yelp, Venue is a Toronto-based, Accel- and Y Combinator-backed productivity company. As of this enrichment pass Venue publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface — this profile captures its identity, website properties, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Wishup
providers.description: Wishup is a remote-work outsourcing platform that matches businesses with pre-vetted virtual assistants, bookkeepers, and automation specialists, typically onboarding a trained professional within 60 minutes. Its managed talent handles inbox and calendar management, CRM and social-media work, bookkeeping, project management, and AI-driven workflow automation across industries such as healthcare, e-commerce, real estate, startups, nonprofits, and legal services. Wishup runs a client-facing Employee Management App for task tracking and real-time feedback, but publishes no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Alcove
providers.description: Alcove is an AI-powered procurement and project management platform built for interior designers, contractors, event planners, and purchasing agents. It consolidates product details, quotes, financials, and order tracking into a single hub, automatically tracking orders across vendors and projects, managing tasks and timelines, calculating profitability and markups, and offering a purchasing service with Designer Net discounts. An AI assistant surfaces financial insights, suggests markups, reviews approvals, and powers filtering. Alcove is a Menlo Ventures portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing site and web application but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: plancraft
providers.description: plancraft is a German cloud-based business management software for craftspeople and trades businesses (Handwerk). It digitizes administrative workflows end to end — quote and estimate creation, project planning, time tracking, on-site documentation, material and labor costing, and invoicing — inside one integrated platform aimed at small and mid-sized construction and trade companies. plancraft supports DATEV export for tax/accounting workflows and DATANORM and GAEB catalog imports for material data and tender processing. It is a venture-backed SaaS company (portfolio company of Creandum). As of this enrichment pass plancraft publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface — integrations are delivered as prebuilt connectors and standardized file-format import/export.

providers.name: WalkMe
providers.description: WalkMe is a Digital Adoption Platform delivering in-app guidance, walkthroughs, and analytics that help users navigate and adopt enterprise applications.

providers.name: 410 Labs
providers.description: 410 Labs is a lean product studio based in Baltimore, Maryland, founded in 2010 by Dave Troy and Matthew Koll with the mission of helping people communicate and access information in new and better ways. The company is best known for Mailstrom, a web-based inbox management and email cleanup tool that groups messages by sender, subject, time, and size so users can act on thousands of related emails at once across Gmail, Google Workspace, Outlook, Apple, AOL, Exchange, and any IMAP mail service. 410 Labs also built the Chuck iPhone app for fast on-the-go email triage, and earlier products Shortmail and Replyz. It is a consumer productivity software company that does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web properties for the API Evangelist network. 410 Labs was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Letswork
providers.description: Letswork is a Dubai-headquartered flexible workspace booking platform that lets members work from coworking spaces, cafes, hotels, meeting rooms, private offices and creative studios through a single credit-based monthly membership with no long-term contract. Founded in 2019 by Omar AlMheiri and Hamza Khan, the platform covers 1030+ workspaces across 63+ cities in 18+ countries, serving 80,000+ members across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa. The product ships as iOS, Android and web apps with one-tap check-in, day passes, hourly meeting-room booking, a private-offices marketplace, and team plans that add a shared credit pool, admin dashboard and usage analytics for hybrid companies. Letswork publishes no public developer API or developer portal; it does publish a first-party llms.txt canonical fact set for AI assistants.

providers.name: AWST
providers.description: AWST is the software company behind WorkRamen, a productivity and business-operations platform aimed at small and medium businesses, startups, agencies, and freelancers. WorkRamen brings meeting scheduling (with Google Calendar and Outlook sync, plus Google Meet and Zoom), trackable document sharing, secure e-signatures, routing forms, visitor management, and Stripe-based payment acceptance into a single workspace. AWST is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a SaaS product only — its brand domain awst.io redirects to workramen.com, and no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or API documentation surface could be found.

providers.name: Billables Ai
providers.description: Billables AI is a San Francisco based legal technology company that builds AI-powered automatic time tracking software for lawyers, consultants, and professional services firms. Its platform passively captures billable activity as people work across the tools they already use — Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, Zoom, Adobe, and the Chrome and Edge browsers — then uses AI to draft time entries, assign the correct client and matter, and write narrative descriptions, learning and adapting to each user over time. Privacy is user-controlled, with only the individual able to view or edit their own time records before they are submitted. The company is venture-backed (Series A) and was surfaced through the Wing Venture Capital portfolio.

providers.name: Pillar
providers.description: Pillar is an Italian construction-technology company, founded in 2025 and headquartered in Milan, building what it calls the operating system for the construction industry (il sistema operativo per l'edilizia). Its cloud platform unifies the back office of building firms (imprese edili) — invoicing (fatturazione), cash-flow management (flussi di cassa), bank reconciliation, quotes and estimates (preventivi), procurement, job and project cost control (gestione commessa), and delivery notes and site work reports (DDT e rapportini) — alongside on-site safety (Pillar Sicurezza) and an AI layer (Pillar AI) that automates data entry in real time, including inputs captured from the job site over WhatsApp. Pillar is backed by Earlybird Venture Capital and today reaches customers through a book-a-demo model rather than a public self-serve signup or a developer-facing API; no public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Please
providers.description: Please (Please Platforms) is an AI-powered "thinking" reminders application for iOS that lets people capture a thought, a link, or an image with zero effort, then automatically enriches each reminder with additional context and surfaces intelligent, connected suggestions so nothing gets missed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Please ships a consumer mobile product and publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Corca
providers.description: Corca is an AI-native, collaborative workspace for mathematics — a browser-based editor that lets people write math naturally (without special syntax), run calculations in real time, and collaborate the way teams do in Figma or Google Docs. Typing keywords like "sum" or "integral" surfaces the right symbols and functions, documents import from and export to LaTeX, and built-in AI helps solve problems, manipulate expressions, and generate code without switching tools. It is used for lab research, lecture creation, team knowledge bases, and publishing academic work. Founded in 2023 and based in New York, Corca raised a $7.8M round (led by NEA, with Bloomberg Beta, NVIDIA's NVentures, Daft Capital, Slow Ventures, Liquid 2, Path Ventures, and Mana Ventures). The product is a consumer/team SaaS application; no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Concepts
providers.description: Concepts is a digital sketching and design application built by TopHatch, Inc., offering an infinite, flexible canvas for thinking, planning, illustration, and design across iOS, Android, and Windows. It blends vector and raster drawing with precision tools, adjustable brushes, layers, and a dynamic tool wheel aimed at designers, illustrators, architects, and product teams. Concepts was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer creative application it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or agent surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web properties along with a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Fluor
providers.description: Fluor Corporation (NYSE: FLR) is a Fortune 500 engineering, procurement, construction and maintenance company headquartered in Irving, Texas. Fluor designs and builds capital projects and provides project-management services for energy, chemicals, life sciences, mining and metals, advanced technologies, infrastructure and government clients worldwide, and licenses its own process technologies such as Econamine FG Plus and Fluor Solvent. Fluor sells engineering and construction services rather than software: it operates no developer program, publishes no API reference, and serves no machine-readable API contract. Its business-to-business integration with suppliers runs inside SAP Ariba and Workday, whose contracts belong to those vendors. This is an independent API Evangelist profile of Fluor's public surface.

providers.name: Presentations.ai
providers.description: Presentations.ai is an AI-powered presentation platform that turns ideas, documents, and data into professional, on-brand slide decks in minutes and exports fully editable PowerPoint files. The product markets programmatic deck generation via a REST API and webhooks, no-code Zapier and Make connectors, white-label embedding, and data-source connections to Salesforce, HubSpot, Google Sheets, Snowflake, and 50+ others, though it publishes no public developer documentation or API reference. Backed by Accel, the company operates under Singapore terms of service.

providers.name: Slidebean
providers.description: Slidebean is a pitch deck and financial modeling platform for startup founders. It combines AI-powered presentation software that auto-designs investor-ready slides with professional pitch deck design services and financial modeling assistance for fundraising. Founders use Slidebean to build, refine, and share pitch decks, model their startup finances, and prepare for investor conversations. As of this enrichment pass Slidebean operates as a consumer/SMB SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal; its GitHub organization contains only forks and small internal JavaScript utilities.

providers.name: Waterfall
providers.description: Waterfall is a sequential software development methodology where progress flows steadily downward through defined phases including requirements, system design, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance. It emphasizes thorough documentation, fixed-scope planning, and phase-gate reviews before proceeding to subsequent stages. Waterfall remains widely used in regulated industries, government contracting, and projects with well-understood, stable requirements.

providers.name: Avec
providers.description: Avec is a free, AI-powered email application for Gmail, built by Nearly Extraterrestrial Technology, Inc. The iOS app prioritizes a user's inbox and surfaces important messages one at a time in a card-based interface, learning individual preferences over time so the most relevant email rises to the top. Users swipe to mark messages done or save them for later, compose replies by voice in their own writing style, receive smart notifications with email summaries, and search their mailbox with natural-language AI. Founded in 2024 by CEO Jonathan Unikowski and backed at seed stage by Bloomberg Beta and Lightspeed Venture Partners, Avec is a consumer productivity product rather than an API provider - it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Parspec
providers.description: Parspec is an AI-native platform for electrical, lighting, and MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) distributors and manufacturer rep agencies in the construction supply chain. It consolidates fragmented, manual workflows into one system covering quoting for complex projects, automated submittal and O&M document creation, project management (orders, fulfillment, billing), and sales management, with ERP integrations (Epicor Eclipse, Epicor Prophet 21, SAP). Parspec is SOC 2 Type II attested and markets itself to help distributors and rep agencies bid more, win more, and improve profitability. Backed by Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: Boomerang
providers.description: Boomerang, from Baydin Inc, is a productivity software company founded in 2010 that builds email management and meeting scheduling tools. Its products include Boomerang for Gmail and Boomerang for Outlook browser extensions, Boomerang mobile apps for iOS and Android, and GQueues, a task manager for Google Workspace teams. Boomerang lets users schedule email to send later, snooze messages back to the inbox, track responses with read receipts and follow-up reminders, share availability and book meetings without back-and-forth, and use AI writing assistance. With over 2 million active customers, the platform has processed more than 500 million messages. Boomerang is a consumer and team-facing productivity suite delivered as browser extensions and apps rather than a developer API platform; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Double
providers.description: Double is a New York-based future-of-work company that pairs busy executives and founders with highly vetted, US-based remote executive assistants, augmented by an AI copilot (Mingo) that helps assistants summarize tasks, draft communications, prompt follow-up questions, and report time. Founded in 2018 by the former Sunrise Calendar team (Alice Default, Christophe Lamperti, Pierre-Elie Fauche), Double delivers operations, marketing, scheduling, inbox, and administrative delegation through a managed platform and shared secure workflows built around a per-client 1Password vault. Double is not a public API provider; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Ajax
providers.description: Ajax is an AI-powered timekeeping platform built specifically for law firms. It automatically captures attorney work across applications, documents, emails, phone calls, and video meetings, then generates OCG-compliant, voice-matched time-entry narratives and syncs them with one click to practice-management and billing systems. Ajax integrates with SurePoint, Clio, MyCase, Filevine, PracticePanther, Centerbase, Actionstep, and Soluno, and positions itself around recovering otherwise-lost billable hours. The company is SOC 2 aligned, encrypts data in transit and at rest, does not train models on customer data, and enforces rolling data deletion. Ajax is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface — it is a product/SaaS company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Avoice
providers.description: Avoice is an AI-native workspace for architects and engineers that automates the non-design work of running an architectural practice. Its AI agents understand drawings, specifications, schedules, materials, building codes, and research to generate specs, run automated QA/QC quality control on specs and drawings, auto-produce door/window/finish schedules and quantities, draft RFIs and submittals for construction administration, and manage a client portal alongside searchable detail and material libraries. A Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, Avoice positions itself as the operating system for architectural practice, with firms managing over $300 million in active projects using it across five countries. Avoice publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation at this time; this profile tracks the company as a network lead.

providers.name: Foresight
providers.description: Foresight is a predictive project-delivery platform for complex construction and infrastructure megaprojects, with a particular focus on data centers, government, and critical infrastructure. Founded by Dr. Atif Ansar and Igor Shifrin (Oxford) and headquartered in London, it layers on top of existing scheduling tools such as Microsoft Project and Excel to turn raw schedule data into forecasts, risk assessment, delay prediction, and portfolio-wide project assurance. The company reports managing $100B+ in mission-critical projects and is backed by Creandum and Macquarie Capital. Foresight is delivered as a SaaS web application and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Happy5
providers.description: Happy5 is a Jakarta-based employee performance management platform, operated by Happy5 For The World Pte. Ltd. and founded in 2013, that unifies goal and OKR management, project tracking, and 360-degree performance reviews in one tool for HR teams. It automatically surfaces the goals hit, projects delivered, and milestones completed inside every performance review, and integrates with tools teams already use such as Jira, Asana, Slack, and Google Sheets. Its customers span major Indonesian banks, startups, and SMEs. Happy5 is a closed SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; this profile captures its verified public identity and web properties as a lead.

providers.name: INBOTIQA
providers.description: INBOTIQA is a UK-based fintech whose flagship product, YUDOmail, is an Intelligent Business Email and shared-mailbox management platform for high-volume group inboxes at banks, BPOs and financial-services operations teams. YUDOmail layers over Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace to turn incoming emails into assigned, trackable tasks with ownership, due dates, SLA tracking, machine-learning triage and sentiment analysis, audit trails and analytics, without replacing the underlying email platform. It deploys in the cloud or on-premises, integrates with Symphony chat and Microsoft Teams, and is used across KYC, FX, collateral, settlements and trade-support functions. INBOTIQA was a 2019 Barclays Accelerator (powered by Techstars) company.

providers.name: Magic
providers.description: Magic, Inc. is a Y Combinator-backed virtual assistant company that matches busy professionals, executives, and entrepreneurs with dedicated, vetted human assistants rather than AI bots. Through its Magic Match screening (assistants drawn from the top 0.5% of applicants), Magic 24/7 backup coverage, and ongoing training, the service handles email and inbox management, calendar and scheduling, travel planning, customer support, research, data entry, and other recurring business and personal tasks. Magic is a consumer- and business-facing staffing/concierge service delivered through a web workspace; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Basebuild
providers.description: Basebuild Labs, Inc. builds Beams, an AI project manager for construction and real estate teams. The product automatically transcribes project meetings, tracks decisions and action items, and assembles a searchable knowledge base from those discussions, capturing information without requiring a bot to join the call. It is aimed at giving construction and real estate project teams real-time visibility and control over teams, projects, budgets, and finances. Basebuild is an early-stage Canaan Partners portfolio company based in Santa Monica, California, and this API Evangelist profile tracks its public-facing surface. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site and a product login only, with no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or documentation surface to catalog.

providers.name: Marker
providers.description: Marker is a writing tool for people who believe in writing — a calm, focused space for thinking and writing that acts as your partner and editor from first idea to final draft. Backed by Index Ventures, Marker sits in the future-of-work space and offers a distraction-free web application (my.marker.page) for drafting long-form writing. It is a consumer product web app: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface, so this profile captures its identity and a live domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Ray Browser
providers.description: Ray Browser is an AI-powered web browser that learns a user's interests and browsing habits to personalize their internet experience. It ships a built-in agent that can run web searches and automate tasks, a curated daily Discover feed, and Ray Studio for building custom tools and dashboards without writing code. The product is currently in public beta with a free Starter plan that grants weekly credits for its AI features. Ray Browser is a consumer product; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking and enrichment.

providers.name: Vela
providers.description: Vela is an AI scheduling assistant from Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch that handles the ambiguity that breaks scheduling. Added to any email thread or messaging conversation, it negotiates on the user's behalf — reading context, proposing meeting times across timezones, following up with participants, detecting calendar conflicts, rescheduling, and sending invites once scheduling is finalized. It works across Gmail, Outlook, Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, SMS, and phone, and is used by enterprise recruiters coordinating thousands of multi-party interviews a week as well as executives who need white-glove coordination at scale.

providers.name: CoConstruct
providers.description: CoConstruct is a residential construction management software platform originally founded in 2005 in Charlottesville, Virginia by Donny Wyatt to help custom home builders and remodelers manage projects, budgets, selections, client communications, scheduling, and financial workflows in a single web and mobile application. The product served thousands of custom builders across the United States and was paired with CBUSA, a homebuilder group purchasing organization CoConstruct previously acquired. On February 24, 2021, CoConstruct was acquired by Buildertrend of Omaha, Nebraska, with growth funding from Bain Capital Tech Opportunities, HGGC, and Serent Capital, creating a combined company serving 23,000+ clients, 1.1M+ users, and $200B+ in annual construction project value. By 2022 Buildertrend had merged the two products into a single unified Buildertrend platform and migrated CoConstruct customers off the legacy product. CoConstruct historically operated a developer portal at developer.coconstruct.com exposing APIs for project, financial, and scheduling data, but as of the merger CoConstruct has paused new API development — "we are not establishing new API endpoints or connecting additional users to existing endpoints" — and the developer portal now redirects to a static notice page. Existing API connections are reportedly maintained but no public OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source release is published. Net-new integration work is directed to Buildertrend's own platform and partner program.

providers.name: Nomad Homes
providers.description: Nomad Homes is a Partech-backed proptech company originally launched as a real-estate marketplace. It has since rebranded and pivoted to RemyAI (getremy.ai) — "the 24/7 intelligent assistant for real estate agents." RemyAI listens to agents' calls and texts, transcribes and summarizes them, auto-creates follow-up tasks and reminders, organizes buyer/seller contacts, and manages voicemail across iOS, Android, and desktop. The company's original domain nomadhomes.co now 301-redirects to getremy.ai. RemyAI publishes a public /.well-known/ai-plugin.json and an llms.txt describing the product, but it exposes NO public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or developer portal (its ai-plugin manifest explicitly declares api.type=none and auth.type=none).

providers.name: Workhelix
providers.description: Workhelix is an enterprise platform for measuring and growing the return on investment of AI initiatives. Its Nucleus product connects workforce data and AI usage history to rank AI opportunities by impact, identify high-performing superusers, surface adoption gaps, and estimate time and cost savings. The company was co-founded by economists Erik Brynjolfsson (Stanford) and Andrew McAfee (MIT) with CEO James Milin and research director Daniel Rock (Wharton), is backed by Bloomberg Beta, and serves enterprise customers including Autodesk, Nasdaq, and LogicMonitor. Workhelix publishes no public API or developer program as of July 2026.

providers.name: Sketchpro
providers.description: SketchPro is an AI copilot for Autodesk Revit that helps architects and engineers automate construction documentation directly inside their live project models. Delivered as a native Revit plugin (not a public developer API), it executes natural-language instructions to handle dimensioning, tagging, view creation, sheet setup, and scheduling, while adapting to each firm's standards, naming conventions, and documentation logic through an admin-configured AI Knowledge Base. Founded in 2023 and used by architecture practices including SOM, 10 Design, and Little, SketchPro is backed by Khosla Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or event/webhook surface; API access is described as "contact vendor / not publicly documented."

providers.name: Instruct
providers.description: Instruct ("AI that works for you") is an AI automation platform that lets non-technical users delegate repetitive work across their connected applications. Users describe a task in natural language and Instruct's AI pulls context from one integrated app, acts on it in another, and can turn any successful one-off task into a recurring scheduled workflow, spanning use cases across education, recruiting, sales, and operations. It is a hosted end-user application with a free plan and Google/email sign-up. As of this profile Instruct does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. Instruct is backed by Creandum.

providers.name: Time is Ltd
providers.description: Time is Ltd. is a collaboration analytics company that turns workplace communication and productivity data into actionable insights for HR, sales, and operations teams. Its platform connects to tools such as Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom, Salesforce, Webex, and Tableau to measure meetings, focus time, and collaboration patterns, then reports on team performance, employee engagement, and revenue outcomes. Backed by Accel and profiled in the API Evangelist network, Time is Ltd. exposes no public developer API; integrations are configured through its hosted analytics application rather than a documented REST or GraphQL surface.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Baseframe
providers.description: BaseFrame (baseframe.co) is a Y Combinator (W26) startup building an AI workflow discovery platform for teams and small businesses. Its privacy-first desktop application analyzes historical work patterns across email, documents, Slack, calendar, browser activity, and files using on-device local models to identify high-value, repetitive tasks and recommend concrete AI automations, then helps users set them up in the tools they already use. BaseFrame publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time; it is a consumer/desktop product with SaaS integrations (Gmail, Slack, HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Sheets, Office 365, Jira). Founded in 2025 by Anshul Paul and Vaibhav Agrawal.

providers.name: Agile Delivery
providers.description: A collection of resources, tools, and APIs related to agile delivery practices — the iterative approach to project management and software delivery that helps teams ship value faster through sprints, continuous feedback, and adaptive planning. Agile delivery frameworks emphasize cross-functional collaboration, working software over documentation, and responding to change over following a plan. This topic covers project management APIs, sprint planning tools, backlog management platforms, and delivery metrics services used to implement agile delivery at scale.

providers.name: Agile SDLC
providers.description: A collection of resources, tools, and APIs covering the Agile Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) — an iterative and incremental approach to software development that integrates agile principles across every phase from requirements through deployment. Agile SDLC replaces the rigid waterfall model with continuous planning, development, testing, and delivery through short sprint cycles. This topic covers the APIs and platforms that support each phase of the agile SDLC including requirements management, code review, CI/CD, testing, and deployment.

providers.name: Google Vids
providers.description: Google Vids is an AI-powered video creation and editing application in Google Workspace that enables business users to produce professional videos without design expertise by combining Gemini-assisted outlining, Veo 3 generative video clips, AI avatars, recording studio capabilities, and a royalty-free stock media library. Vids is available on Business and Enterprise Workspace plans as well as Google AI Pro and Ultra consumer plans, with collaboration handled through standard Workspace sharing controls. There is no public developer REST API for Google Vids at this time; this index tracks the product as a documentation-only reference.

providers.name: Poly
providers.description: Poly is an AI-powered intelligent cloud file browser that syncs a user's local files to the cloud and layers an AI agent over them, letting people search by image, concept, phrase, color or face and ask natural-language questions about their documents, images, video and audio to get summaries, transcriptions, tags and generated content such as podcasts and presentations. Founded by CEO Abhay Agarwal, Poly (formerly reached at withpoly.com, now poly.app) emerged from stealth in November 2025 with $8M in seed funding led by Felicis with participation from Bloomberg Beta, NextView, Figma Ventures, AI Grant, Wing Ventures and MVP Ventures. It is currently in waitlist/beta on web and Mac, with a Windows version planned, and as of this enrichment pass publishes no public developer API, SDKs, CLI, or MCP server.

providers.name: Brick&Bolt
providers.description: Brick&Bolt (bricknbolt.com) is a Bangalore-based, tech-enabled home and commercial construction marketplace that delivers end-to-end design-to-build services across major Indian cities including Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Delhi NCR, and Mysuru. The company connects homeowners with vetted contractors and manages projects through its QASCON quality system (470+ quality checks), an ESCROW-secured payment model that releases funds only as milestones complete, transparent quotations, and consumer and professional mobile apps for real-time project tracking. Backed by Accel, Brick&Bolt has delivered thousands of homes and was named to Forbes Asia's "100 to Watch" list. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Brick&Bolt operates a consumer construction platform and mobile apps but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Crew
providers.description: Crew is a digital workplace platform for frontline and deskless teams, connecting frontline staff to corporate leadership across distributed workforces. The product bundles real-time team communication and employee engagement, labor optimization and shift scheduling, task execution, culture and recognition, knowledge management, a Command Center for administration and analytics, a compliance and safety suite, and third-party integrations. Crew reports serving more than one million frontline workers across companies including Taco Bell, Wendy's, Planet Fitness, and Harps Foods. It is backed by Greylock and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Focused Space, Inc.
providers.description: Focused Space, Inc. operates focused.space, a consumer productivity platform built around "body doubling" — a neuroscience-backed technique where people work silently alongside others to more easily enter and sustain a flow state. The service combines 100+ weekly live sessions hosted by real humans (available 24/7) with a custom focus-video platform, a goal-setting and task-tracking app, and a community aimed at creatives, builders, remote workers, and people with ADHD. Focused Space is a 500 Global (and E14 Fund) portfolio company. It ships web, iOS, and Android apps but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its public web and security posture.

providers.name: OnsiteIQ
providers.description: OnsiteIQ is a construction intelligence platform for real estate owners and developers that combines regular on-site 360-degree reality capture with AI-powered computer vision to monitor construction progress across trades and asset classes. The platform documents projects visually week over week, turns the imagery into searchable, measurable records, and surfaces analytics and actionable insights that teams use to verify progress, support payment applications, and make business-critical decisions on projects anywhere in the world. OnsiteIQ is a private company headquartered in New York City and backed by Anthemis and Bullpen Capital. As surfaced through the API Evangelist network, OnsiteIQ publishes a marketing and product website but does not expose a public developer API, documentation portal, or machine-readable API surface at this time; this profile records that honest state alongside the company's identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Saturn
providers.description: Saturn is a mobile calendar and scheduling app built for high school students, designed around the complexities of the school day, built around your friends, and kept truly real-time. Students import their class schedule, see what their friends are doing, coordinate activities, and share their calendar socially. The company positions itself as "the next generation calendar, enabling time together for all." Saturn is a consumer iOS and Android application distributed through the App Store and Google Play; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. Backed by General Catalyst and Insight Partners, with notable individual investors including Jeff Bezos, Marc Benioff, and Dara Khosrowshahi.

providers.name: Dooly
providers.description: Dooly was a connected workspace for revenue teams that improved Salesforce CRM hygiene by syncing meeting notes, pipeline updates, and next steps back into Salesforce automatically. It layered a fast note-taking surface, deal vitals, real-time playbooks, and one-click CRM updates on top of Salesforce so account executives could keep their pipeline clean without manual data entry. Backed by Battery Ventures, Dooly was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. The Dooly platform was shut down on June 30, 2025; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, and this profile captures the remaining public surface (website, privacy policy, terms) for the record.

providers.name: Agile
providers.description: A collection of resources, standards, and APIs representing the broader agile landscape — the set of software development principles first codified in the 2001 Agile Manifesto. Agile values individuals and interactions over processes and tools, working software over comprehensive documentation, customer collaboration over contract negotiation, and responding to change over following a plan. This topic index covers the full ecosystem of agile frameworks, methodologies, tools, and APIs including Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, XP, and Lean.

providers.name: Agile Methodology
providers.description: A collection of resources, standards, and APIs related to agile methodology — the set of principles and frameworks that guide modern software development. Agile methodologies including Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, and XP emphasize iterative delivery, customer collaboration, and adaptability. This topic covers the ecosystem of project management APIs, ceremony-facilitation tools, and metrics platforms that teams use to implement agile methodology in practice.

providers.name: Buildertrend
providers.description: Buildertrend is an Omaha, Nebraska-based cloud construction-management platform serving residential home builders, remodelers, and specialty trade contractors. The product consolidates sales (CRM, leads, proposals, contracts, email marketing), project management (schedule, daily logs, selections, change orders, warranties, sub portal, client updates), and financial management (estimates, bids, takeoff, job-costing budgets, bills, purchase orders, invoices, online payments) into a single web and mobile application used by 20,000+ builders. Pricing is custom-quoted by sales rather than published self-serve tiers, with unlimited users and projects on every plan, and the platform integrates with QuickBooks, Xero, and other accounting and trade tools through a partner integrations marketplace. The company exposes a REST API at api.buildertrend.com that is gated by partner agreement — endpoints return 401 Unauthorized to the public and there is no open developer portal, public OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API key signup. As a result Buildertrend is profiled here as a non-public (partner-only) API provider; the public surface documented is limited to marketing, support, integrations marketplace, mobile apps, and corporate resources.

providers.name: Heyclicky
providers.description: Heyclicky (product name Clicky) is a consumer macOS application from the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch that puts an AI assistant right next to your cursor. In Talk Mode a hotkey lets you ask about whatever is on screen and get spoken, on-screen guidance; in Agent Mode you can command autonomous agents to build, research, or perform tasks in the background, and it can connect to services like Notion, Gmail, and Calendar. The app is screen-aware, works across any application with no plugins, and ships as a notarized macOS binary distributed via a Sparkle appcast on GitHub. Heyclicky is a consumer desktop product; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: getriff
providers.description: Riff (getriff.co) is a voice and video workspace for remote and hybrid teams, backed by Balderton Capital. Its Mac and Windows desktop apps aim to reduce Slack overload and Zoom fatigue with a minimal video header, one-click availability-based chat, multi-screen sharing with drawing tools, advanced echo cancellation, and focus-time scheduling that updates status automatically, plus Google Calendar and Slack integrations. Riff ships as a consumer/team desktop product and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI; this API Evangelist profile captures its identity, legal, and domain-security surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital.

providers.name: Teap
providers.description: Teap is a collaboration and productivity platform providing APIs for workspace management, team coordination, real-time notifications, and analytics. The platform offers core REST APIs for managing users, workspaces, and tasks, along with webhook support for event-driven integrations and analytics endpoints for workspace insights.

providers.name: iControl
providers.description: iControl is a Swedish construction-technology company whose mobile application digitalizes documentation on construction sites, replacing paper-based protocols and inspection records with real-time digital capture. Field personnel create, share, and manage project documentation from the job site, with offline capture that syncs when connectivity returns, drawing and blueprint uploads, and team collaboration. Marketed under the promise "Skriv aldrig ett protokoll igen" (never write a protocol again), iControl is used by leading Nordic contractors including NCC, JM, Veidekke, ARCONA, and In3prenor across infrastructure, residential, commercial, and public-facility projects. The company is headquartered in Stockholm and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. iControl exposes a consumer-facing web and mobile application; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Microsoft Project APIs
providers.description: A collection of APIs for Microsoft Project, enabling project management, task tracking, resource allocation, and collaboration capabilities.

providers.name: Vercept
providers.description: Vercept is an AI startup building AI that works directly on your computer rather than in a distant cloud — software that understands your screen, workflows, and intent and can act on your behalf safely and transparently. Its product, Vy, is a personal computer AI assistant offered as a paid subscription. Vercept was founded by Kiana Ehsani, Luca Weihs, and Ross Girshick, backed by Point Nine, Fifty Years, AI2 Incubator, and Madrona, and was acquired by Anthropic in early 2026. Vercept does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Knowify
providers.description: Knowify is a New York-based construction management SaaS for trade contractors (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, painting, remodeling, concrete, excavation), covering the full job lifecycle from bidding through payment on a single platform. The product spans project execution (estimating, proposals and contracts, change orders, RFIs and submittals, scheduling, daily logs, document and photo management), service work (dispatch, invoicing, payments, field operations, asset and inventory management), and financial management (AIA billing, job costing, prevailing wage, purchase orders, expenses, WIP and reporting).
