Knowify is positioned as the official construction software partner of QuickBooks Online and offers deep two-way sync with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, Intuit Enterprise Suite, QuickBooks Payroll, QuickBooks Payments, and QuickBooks Time, alongside native integrations with CompanyCam, Billd, Lumber, eBacon, and AIA Contract Documents. Third-party automation is available via Zapier. Pricing starts at $99/month (Core), $249/month (Advanced), and custom Enterprise, with paid add-ons for Service Pro, Live Equipment Tracking (FleetSharp), AI Dashcams, and Tool Tracking. Knowify does not publish a public REST API, webhooks specification, SDK, CLI, or developer portal; programmatic access for third parties is limited to Zapier and the QuickBooks ecosystem.

providers.name: Craftview
providers.description: Craftview Software GmbH is a Frankfurt-headquartered European software group that builds ERP and project-management software for the skilled trades. Formed as a buy-and-build platform, Craftview operates a portfolio of long-established regional ERP brands — C'FLUIDE, ES2000, EXTRABAT, GILDE, KS21, MOSER, OSD, PLENION, RITA BOSSE and WINWORKER — serving green industries, construction-related trades, technical services and specialized crafts across Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands and France. The group reports 25,000+ active customers, 330+ employees and 11 locations across 41 key European regions. Craftview publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API definitions; its software is sold and delivered per brand as on-premise and cloud ERP for trade businesses.

providers.name: Subset
providers.description: Subset is an AI-powered spreadsheet editor built for finance professionals, letting them generate P&L statements from PDFs, build DCF and returns models, and process CIMs and teasers through natural-language instructions inside a familiar spreadsheet interface. Built in NYC and SF by former Wall Street professionals, Subset targets investment and financial-modeling workflows. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Subset ships a consumer/prosumer web application and help documentation but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Jarvie
providers.description: Jarvie is a consumer AI assistant from All Day Technologies, Inc. that lives inside iMessage and SMS group chats. Marketed as "your group chat sidekick," it helps people who text together plan events, learn things, and have fun, and can draft emails and create calendar events on a user's behalf. It offers memory features to personalize responses across conversations. Jarvie is a mobile-messaging consumer product surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners; as of this profile it does not publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Lean Six Sigma Black Belt
providers.description: Lean Six Sigma Black Belt is an advanced certification in Lean Six Sigma methodology focused on leading complex improvement projects, statistical analysis, and change management to reduce defects and variability in business processes.

providers.name: Buildots
providers.description: Buildots is an AI-powered construction intelligence platform headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, with offices in London and the United States. The company combines 360-degree hardhat-mounted cameras with computer vision and machine learning models that automatically capture, locate, and classify on-site construction progress against the project BIM model and schedule, producing trade-level performance data, deviation and delay detection, and portfolio-wide analytics for general contractors, project teams, executives, and owners. Buildots reports that projects using the platform together with a performance-driven operating approach have reduced delays by up to 50%. The product family includes Buildots (the AI construction intelligence platform), Genda (workforce intelligence), and a fully managed Capture Services operation that handles routine site capture for customers. Verticals served include data centers, commercial, multifamily, healthcare, industrial, education, and airports. Notable customers shown on the website include Intel, Mortenson, JE Dunn, Turner, Wates, and STO. Buildots was founded in 2018 and is led by CEO and co-founder Roy Danon with co-founders Aviv Leibovici (CPO) and Yakir Sudry (CCO). Investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners, Future Energy Ventures, Viola Ventures, TLV Partners, OG Ventures, and Tencent. Buildots does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integrations with construction software (e.g., Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud) are arranged directly through the company.

providers.name: Stack
providers.description: Stack is a spatial web browser that organizes the web as cards on a canvas rather than rows of tabs, built for keyboard-first, distraction-free browsing. Features include Fly Mode for fast navigation, multiple user profiles, customizable visual themes called realms, Chrome extension support, and privacy-focused browsing without ads or trackers, with multiplayer collaboration planned. Stack is a consumer desktop application and does not currently publish a public API, developer platform, or SDK. Backed by 500 Global and community-funded via WeFunder.

providers.name: Town
providers.description: Town is a personal AI assistant that works across email, calendar, Slack, docs, WhatsApp, and the web. Users connect their accounts and Town — through a personal agent called a "Townie" — learns how they work, then suggests and runs automated "routines" (meeting briefs, email drafting, follow-ups, scheduling) on their behalf. Founded by Jean-Denis Greze (former Plaid CTO) and Tony Vincent (former Google product/AI lead), Town raised a $55M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (June 2026) with Forerunner Ventures, First Round, Alt Capital, and Conviction participating. Town publishes no public developer program: the product is fully auth-gated, api.town.com is a Convex backend deployment rather than a public API, and its robots.txt carries explicit Content-Signal declarations restricting AI training on its content.

providers.name: Sandbar
providers.description: Sandbar is a consumer hardware and AI company behind Stream, a private voice ring and conversational notes app. Worn on the finger, Stream pairs a discreet private microphone, a glass touchpad, and silent haptics with an on-device "Inner Voice" assistant so people can capture notes, reminders, and todos, dictate speech-to-text across any iOS or Mac app, and think aloud without reaching for a phone. Backed by Kindred Ventures and True Ventures, Sandbar is a preorder-stage consumer product; it publishes a marketing site, an About/Us page, and a Careers page, but no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Crunched
providers.description: Crunched is an AI Excel analyst for power users in management consulting, investment banking, private equity, and corporate finance. Working as a native Microsoft Excel add-in (Mac and PC) and a companion PowerPoint deck reviewer, it builds fully linked financial models (DCFs, LBOs, cohort and scenario analyses) from plain-English instructions, error-checks entire workbooks, extracts and structures data from PDFs and web sources, formats spreadsheets, and generates client-ready slides with full workbook context. Every edit is tracked with a full audit trail and cited sources. Founded by Philip Borge and Michael Sakowski (ex-McKinsey private equity), Crunched is ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR compliant, and is backed by Y Combinator, First Round Capital, and 20VC. It is distributed through the Microsoft AppSource marketplace and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Bitacora.io
providers.description: Bitacora.io is a Mexican field-data and operations platform (a 500 Global / 500 LatAm Batch 14 startup) that helps deskless teams in construction, maintenance, and field services capture reports, photos, tasks, and events from the field. Its mobile and web apps work offline and sync to the cloud when connectivity returns, turning field activity into searchable records, PDF and Excel exports, map and gallery views, and real-time analytics dashboards for managers. Bitacora is a SaaS product rather than a developer-API company - it offers custom development, integrations, and KPI dashboards as professional services, but does not publish a public self-serve API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK.

providers.name: Buildcon
providers.description: Buildcon is a Belgrade-based construction and logistics digitalisation company that builds Buildx, a proprietary construction project management platform covering project scheduling, cost tracking, daily logs, installed-quantities tracking, and reporting, alongside Buildx Warehouse for warehouse management and Buildx Tracking for real-time asset tracking. The team pairs deep construction and logistics domain knowledge with a modern web stack (React, Angular, Node.js, PostgreSQL on AWS/DigitalOcean) to help builders and logistics operators move off spreadsheets and onto connected operational software. Buildcon is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Alien Labs
providers.description: Alien Labs, Inc. was a San Francisco software startup founded by Cristian Strat, Mircea Pasoi and Liana Dumitru, and a seed-stage portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Under the Alien Labs banner the team shipped Summify, a social news digest acquired by Twitter in January 2012, and later Memo — "the wiki that's always up-to-date" — a Slack-native team knowledge base that let 8,000+ teams star a Slack message to save it as a searchable note, edit rich-text and code-block documents in context, and retrieve them with a /memo-find slash command. Memo stopped accepting new signups on January 16, 2018 and shut down on March 16, 2018; most of the engineering team joined Coinbase. The company operates no live developer portal, documentation, or public API today, and this profile is retained as a historical network record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Daero Group
providers.description: DAERO (Daero Group) is a construction-technology company building mobile-first tools for trades and field teams. Its flagship product, ZeroPunch, is a field-operations platform that turns real-time field intuition into structured construction data: voice-first capture lets crews speak field observations in natural language, photos are paired with contextual field data, work is auto-assigned by scope, and stream-of-consciousness notes are converted into organized daily logs. ZeroPunch offers a two-way integration with Procore for project-management sync. The company positions itself around the daily needs of the people actually doing the work, aiming to make construction operations smarter and faster. As of this profile DAERO publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integration is partnership-level (Procore) and inquiries go to support@daerogroup.com. Backed by Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: Emailio
providers.description: Emailio is a Y Combinator (Winter 2014) and Thiel Fellowship-backed startup building "email built for wellness" — a consumer email client for iPhone, iPad, and Mac that centers user wellbeing and mental health rather than traditional inbox-productivity metrics. Its pre-launch landing page describes inbox management, email batching, mood tracking, one-click unsubscribe, and Smart Rule Suggestions, with early access gated behind a waitlist. Founded by Martin Stoyanov and Teo Teodosiev with a roughly five-person team, Emailio sits at the intersection of the productivity and health & wellness categories. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; as of this pass it exposes a consumer product only — no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs could be found.

providers.name: Binary Thumbs
providers.description: Binary Thumbs (operating name "Binary Thumb", Y Combinator Summer 2012) was a San Francisco startup founded in 2012 by Josh Leong, Michael Lin, and Matt Monson to reinvent the spreadsheet for touch devices. Its single product, Grid, was a collaborative grid-based spreadsheet and organizational app for iPad and iPhone that let people keep notes, pictures, people, and places in a freeform grid rather than rigid rows and columns. The company raised roughly $2.15M across a 2012 YC round and a 2013 seed, with participation from angel and institutional investors, and appears on the Andreessen Horowitz public investment list. Y Combinator now lists the company as inactive; Josh Leong led it as CEO from 2012 to 2016. Binary Thumb never shipped a public API, developer portal, or documentation surface -- it was a consumer iOS product company. Its lasting public technical footprint is the BinaryThumb GitHub organization and a handful of open-source React and JavaScript utility libraries published to npm.

providers.name: Xembly
providers.description: Xembly was a Seattle-based enterprise AI company (2020-2024) whose assistant, Xena, acted as an automated "chief of staff" for knowledge workers - scheduling meetings, taking meeting notes, and tracking action items and tasks over email and Slack. Spun out of Madrona Venture Labs by Pete Christothoulou, Jason Flaks, and Peter Francis, and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Norwest Venture Partners ($15M Series A), and Seven Peaks Ventures, Xembly discontinued its customer-facing services on June 1, 2024. It never published a public developer API, and the xembly.com domain has since lapsed to an unrelated operator.

providers.name: Cove
providers.description: Cove is a visual workspace for thinking with AI — an AI collaborator that works alongside you on projects big and small in a spatial, canvas-style interface rather than a linear chat. The product pairs an on-screen agent that can search the web, write and run code, and cite sources with a flexible visual surface for organizing ideas, and it ships an accompanying Chrome browser extension. Cove is a consumer/prosumer application backed by the venture firm Homebrew; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation. This entry tracks Cove in the API Evangelist network, with domain-security posture captured by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Hill International
providers.description: Hill International is a global construction consulting firm founded in 1976 in Mt. Laurel, New Jersey, providing program, project, and construction management, project management oversight, claims and dispute resolution, estimating and cost management, facilities management, project monitoring, troubled project turnaround, commissioning, and project labor agreement consulting to public and private sector owners across more than 100 offices in 42 countries. In December 2022 Hill agreed to be acquired by Global Infrastructure Solutions, Inc. (GISI), the parent of STV, with the take-private transaction closing in May 2023 — Hill now operates as a GISI Consulting Group company alongside STV, GEI Consultants, LiRo-Hill, Layton Construction, and the broader GISI portfolio. Hill International is a professional services firm and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or any developer portal.

providers.name: Hackpad
providers.description: Hackpad was a web-based real-time collaborative wiki and document editor, built on the open-source Etherpad codebase, that let teams write and edit documents together simultaneously. It was acquired by Dropbox in April 2014 and its underlying platform was released as open source under the Apache 2.0 license at github.com/dropbox/hackpad. The hosted hackpad.com service was wound down after Dropbox folded the team's work into Dropbox Paper, and the public service was discontinued in 2017. This API Evangelist profile tracks Hackpad as a historical, now-defunct portfolio company surfaced from the a16z portfolio; there is no live production API surface remaining, and the durable public artifact is the open-source repository.

providers.name: Scrum
providers.description: Scrum is an agile project management framework that organizes work into fixed-length iterations called sprints, typically lasting two to four weeks. It defines clear roles (Product Owner, Scrum Master, Developers) and ceremonies (sprint planning, daily standups, retrospectives) to enable teams to deliver value incrementally and continuously improve.

providers.name: 6 Wunderkinder
providers.description: 6 Wunderkinder (6Wunderkinder GmbH) was a Berlin-based software startup founded in 2010 that built Wunderlist, a popular cross-platform to-do list and task management application. The company shipped a public REST API for Wunderlist in 2013, along with webhooks and integrations such as Slack and Sunrise, and rebuilt its backend into roughly 60 microservices behind a single unified API. Backed by Earlybird and Sequoia Capital, 6 Wunderkinder was acquired by Microsoft in June 2015 for a reported US$100-200M. Microsoft folded the product into Microsoft To Do and discontinued Wunderlist on 6 May 2020. This profile is retained as a historical record; the company is defunct and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Acompli
providers.description: Acompli was a mobile email application for iOS and Android, first released in April 2014, that unified email, calendar, contacts, and file management across Microsoft Exchange, Office 365, Google Apps, Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo, and Outlook.com/Hotmail accounts. The San Francisco startup was backed by Redpoint Ventures and acquired by Microsoft on December 1, 2014 for a reported $200M+, after which its 21-person team and product were rebranded as Microsoft Outlook for iOS and Android. Acompli no longer operates as an independent company and never published a public developer API; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical, acquired-company lead.

providers.name: Astrid *
providers.description: Astrid was a popular cross-platform social to-do list and task-management app (Todoroo, Inc.), known for its Android and web productivity service and a lightweight task-sync API. It was a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the consumer sector. Yahoo acquired the Astrid team in May 2013 and discontinued the service later that year; the astrid.com domain now resolves to Yahoo and the original developer surface (apidoc / api_keys) is dead. The Android client was open-sourced (todoroo/astrid) and later revived by the community as tasks.org (tasks/tasks). No live first-party API, developer portal, or documentation exists to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct portfolio lead.

providers.name: Cofia
providers.description: Cofia is an AI automation platform that learns how a team actually works and automatically builds custom workflow automations without manual setup. By monitoring system events and recognizing repetitive patterns, Cofia proposes and assembles custom agents for tasks like prospect list building, outreach and follow-ups, recruiting pipeline management, and data report creation. The company markets itself as "AI automations that implement themselves." Cofia is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in New York City, founded by Moses Wayne (formerly Engineering Director at Duolingo) and Paola Martinez (formerly Senior Product Manager at Brilliant.org). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with what the company publishes publicly. As of this pass Cofia exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Collaborate *
providers.description: Collaborate.com was a mobile-first team collaboration service — unified document sharing, task management and team messaging across iPhone, iPod Touch, Android and the web, with integrations into Box, Dropbox and Google Drive. It was a service of Boston-based Kibits Corp, founded in 2011 by Matt Cutler (CEO) and David Greenstein (CTO), and was backed by GV (Google Ventures), Charles River Ventures, General Catalyst, SOS Ventures, Commonwealth Capital Ventures and Launch Capital. The company exited via acquisition by Cisco (December 2013), and its collaboration technology was folded into Cisco's communications portfolio. The company no longer operates independently: collaborate.com is now a MarkMonitor-managed redirect that sends plain-HTTP traffic to https://www.webex.com/ and serves nothing over HTTPS. There is no developer portal, documentation, SDK, package, webhook or API surface to catalog — the asterisk in GV's portfolio listing marks the exit.

providers.name: Command E
providers.description: Command E was a universal search startup that built a keyboard-driven (Cmd+E) desktop tool for searching across the cloud applications people use at work — Google Drive, Slack, Notion, email, and more — from a single command bar, returning unified results without switching apps. The company was backed by Amplify Partners in the ai-ml / productivity search space. Command E was acquired by Dropbox in 2021, and its team went on to help build Dropbox Dash. Its former developer/marketing site at getcommande.com no longer resolves, so no live API, OpenAPI, or developer documentation surface is available to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Conjectag
providers.description: Conjectag (Conject AG / Conject Holding GmbH) was a Munich-based German construction technology company founded in 2000 that provided cloud-based software for the built environment, covering project management, collaboration, document control, and construction cost management for the AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) sector. It was surfaced as a historical Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company. Conject was acquired by the Australian construction collaboration platform Aconex in March 2016, and Aconex was subsequently acquired by Oracle in December 2017; the company no longer operates independently and publishes no live website or developer/API surface. This profile is retained for network provenance rather than active enrichment.

providers.name: Core Labs
providers.description: Core Labs is an early-stage product studio based in New York City building the future of professional identity and connection for the digital economy. Founded by serial entrepreneur Ajay Rajani (previously Grovo and Tala), the company operates in rapid-experimentation mode, incubating and testing consumer and productivity products. Its portfolio includes Mural, a simple portfolio-building tool for product managers, marketers, and digital workers that turns shared URLs into rich embeds; Core, a peer-and-expert mentorship platform used in university entrepreneurship programs and fellowships; and Makeshop, an on-demand marketplace for creative services. Core Labs is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform.

providers.name: Crews By Core *
providers.description: Crews by Core was a construction field-execution platform based in Palo Alto, California (with a Tokyo office), founded and led by CEO Di-Ann Eisnor. Branded "Mission Control for the Field," its mobile-first product gave superintendents and foremen a single tool for lookahead scheduling, jobsite logistics, drawings, and field-to-office messaging, layered with AI-driven risk detection to quantify and mitigate schedule and financial risk on the jobsite. The company was backed by GV (Google Ventures) among ten investors and was acquired by construction IoT company WakeCap on July 1, 2024, folding its scheduling and communication tooling into WakeCap's worker-productivity sensor platform. Crews by Core did not expose a public developer API; this profile documents the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dulcetta
providers.description: Dulcetta is the company behind Focus@Will (focusatwill.com), a functional-music streaming service that curates instrumental soundtracks scientifically designed to improve concentration and productivity during focused work. Backed by 500 Global, Dulcetta operates a consumer subscription product marketing measurable gains in focus for knowledge workers, students, and creative professionals who work with music. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced lead; no public developer API or documentation surface has been identified to date, so this profile carries company identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Gantto
providers.description: Gantto was a web-based Gantt chart and project scheduling SaaS launched in August 2010, backed by Y Combinator and 500 Startups (500 Global). It let teams create and share project schedules in the browser as an alternative to Microsoft Project, with a customer base that reportedly included Twitter, Lucasfilm, and Fujitsu. Gantto was acquired by Dutch competitor Tom's Planner on July 9, 2013, and the product was subsequently discontinued, with users migrated to Tom's Planner. gantto.com now redirects to tomsplanner.com. This company is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record; it publishes no developer program, API, or technical surface to enrich.

providers.name: Huddl
providers.description: Huddl (huddl.ai) was an AI meeting-collaboration platform founded in 2017 in Mountain View, California by CEO Krishna Yarlagadda and CTO Nava Davuluri. The product acted as a collaboration hub layered over Zoom, Webex, and Microsoft Teams, using automatic speech recognition to turn meeting audio into searchable text alongside real-time collaborative note-taking and AI-generated meeting summaries. The company raised roughly $8.7M in venture funding. As of this enrichment pass the huddl.ai domain no longer resolves (delegated to Namecheap parking nameservers with no A/AAAA/MX/TXT records), indicating the service is discontinued; no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or GitHub organization could be located.

providers.name: Knote
providers.description: Knote is a small New York-based startup backed by 500 Global, surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. Third-party company databases describe it inconsistently: Tracxn profiles Knote as a knowledge-management platform that raised roughly $150K from 500 Global, while Dealroom describes it as an AI-powered email summarization and management tool. No first-party description could be confirmed. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass the knote.com web property is offline — the domain resolves (Cloudflare nameservers, an EC2 A record, live Google Workspace MX and an SPF record including Mailgun and Mailchimp) but refuses connections on both port 80 and port 443, so no homepage, developer portal, documentation, API reference, or machine-readable specification could be retrieved. No corporate GitHub organization, package-registry client library, or public API surface was found; the GitHub repositories named "Knote" are unrelated third-party note-taking and Kubernetes-course projects. This profile therefore carries only what could be independently verified: the funding and identity facts above plus a live DNS/TLS domain-security probe. It should be treated as a dormant or defunct lead and re-checked if the domain returns to service.

providers.name: Koan
providers.description: Koan was a goal-management SaaS at koan.co that billed itself as "The Free OKR and Status Tracking Platform", pairing OKR goal setting with a weekly "Reflections" status-update loop and an Insights layer so teams tracked progress as a habit rather than a quarterly spreadsheet exercise. The product shipped a Goal Metrics API — enabled per goal via an API integration toggle on the goal edit page — so teams could push their most important numbers into Koan goals in real time, alongside a Zapier app and native integrations with Slack, Jira, and Okta SSO. Koan was acquired by Gtmhub, an acquisition announced on its own homepage and blog by January 2022, and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Uncork Capital portfolio company. As of enrichment the koan.co domain no longer serves the product: it redirects to a GoDaddy domain-for-sale lander, and there is no live developer portal, documentation, API reference, SDK, or status surface left to harvest.

providers.name: Makelog
providers.description: Makelog was a product changelog and release-notes platform that helped software and product teams collect, curate, and publish product updates to communicate releases with customers and internal stakeholders. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment (sector: productivity). As of this enrichment pass the makelog.com domain no longer resolves (DNS NXDOMAIN) and no live web, developer, or API surface could be reached, indicating the product has been discontinued.

providers.name: Multi
providers.description: Multi (originally launched as Remotion in 2019) was a macOS-native multiplayer collaboration application for software teams, offering multi-person screensharing for up to ten participants, shared cursor and keyboard control with sub-100ms latency, session recording, and AI-generated summaries and action items. Backed by Greylock and First Round Capital, the company was acqui-hired by OpenAI in June 2024; the product was shut down and user data deleted, with the founding team joining OpenAI's ChatGPT desktop group. The multi.app site remains live as a static marketing page but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: OFF
providers.description: OFF (Off-Live, off.live) is an enterprise AI software company building intelligent applications that help organizations streamline, innovate, and grow. Its products include AiVee, a smart scheduling assistant that uses computer vision to turn calendar images into digital events and manage invitations across popular calendar apps, and Pumky, a text-to-image generation platform with customizable artistic styles for both beginners and professionals. The company builds on computer vision, multilingual large language models, and domain-specialized AI models. Backed by Coinbase Ventures, Samsung Next, and Electric Capital. Surfaced as a portfolio company of electric-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: OSlash
providers.description: OSlash is a productivity tool that lets teams create short, memorable shortcuts — typed as "o/" followed by a keyword — to instantly find and open their documents, dashboards, and internal tools across 100+ connected apps such as Salesforce, Notion, Jira, GitHub, Figma, Asana, HubSpot, and Linear. Delivered as a Chrome extension with enterprise features like SSO and bank-level encryption, OSlash was backed by Accel. As of this profile the public product is marked "Coming Soon" and the company publishes no developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or documentation surface — this remains an enrichment lead with no scored API artifacts beyond a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Powerplay
providers.description: Powerplay is a construction project management platform built by Coffer Internet Services Pvt. Ltd. (Bengaluru, India) that gives builders, general contractors, subcontractors, project managers, and site engineers mobile and desktop tools to run construction projects end to end: real-time work and progress tracking, material procurement and inventory management, labor attendance and payroll, issue tracking, petty-cash and expense management, and reporting dashboards. The product is delivered primarily through iOS and Android field apps with a desktop companion. Powerplay does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation, so this profile captures its identity and web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Primavera Systems
providers.description: Primavera Systems, Inc. was a project-management and project-portfolio-management software company best known for the Primavera P6 scheduling platform used in construction, engineering, and capital-projects industries. It was acquired by Oracle Corporation in 2008 and folded into Oracle's Construction and Engineering business, where the products live on as Oracle Primavera. As an independent company it no longer exists, its primavera.com domain now redirects to oracle.com/primavera, and it publishes no independent public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation of its own. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead, but that association does not match the acquired-by-Oracle entity and appears to be a name-matching artifact.

providers.name: Product Backlog
providers.description: A product backlog is a prioritized list of features, enhancements, and fixes that serves as the single source of requirements for product development. It is most commonly used in Agile and Scrum methodologies, where the product owner is responsible for ordering items based on business value, customer feedback, dependencies, and technical considerations. The backlog evolves continuously as new requirements emerge and priorities shift, providing development teams with a clear, ordered view of upcoming work.

providers.name: Product Backlog Items
providers.description: Product backlog items (PBIs) are the individual units of work that make up a product backlog, representing features, enhancements, bug fixes, and technical tasks in Agile and Scrum methodologies. Each PBI typically includes a description, acceptance criteria, priority, and an estimate of effort. PBIs are continuously refined through grooming and refinement sessions, and the highest-priority items are pulled into sprints by development teams to be implemented and delivered as increments of working software.

providers.name: Project Management Methodology
providers.description: A systematic approach or framework for planning, executing, and controlling projects to achieve specific goals within defined constraints of time, budget, and resources. It helps teams plan, execute, and deliver projects on time and within scope through structured methodologies.

providers.name: Quickoffice
providers.description: Quickoffice was a mobile office productivity suite (document, spreadsheet, and presentation editing for iOS, Android, and Symbian) that was acquired by Google in June 2012, folded into Google Docs / Google Drive, and formally discontinued in 2014. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 confirmed there is no independent Quickoffice API surface. The quickoffice.com domain now resolves to Google infrastructure and www.quickoffice.com 301-redirects to google.com/docs/about/, developer.quickoffice.com does not resolve (NXDOMAIN), and no developer portal, documentation, or API remains. The product capabilities live on inside Google Workspace (Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides).

providers.name: RACI
providers.description: A responsibility assignment matrix that defines roles and responsibilities using four key designations - Responsible (those who do the work), Accountable (the ultimate decision maker), Consulted (those whose input is needed), and Informed (those who need to be kept updated). RACI matrices help clarify ownership, reduce confusion, and improve project coordination by mapping stakeholders to specific tasks or deliverables.

providers.name: Rodeo
providers.description: Rodeo is a consumer social app that helps people wrangle their social life: save the things you want to do — social posts, screenshots, links and photos — and then do the things you saved together with friends, while Rodeo wrangles the details and keeps you organized. Tagline: "Save it. Do it." Backed by Foundry Group and Seedcamp. As of this enrichment pass Rodeo publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs or .well-known discovery surface — it is a consumer mobile/web product, not an API provider.

providers.name: Streamonce
providers.description: StreamOnce was a cloud-based enterprise collaboration platform founded in 2012 in San Jose, California by Ilan Twig and Ariel Cohen (who later co-founded TripActions/Navan). The product connected business systems into a social enterprise layer so teams could reply to emails, read documents, and post to Yammer and Chatter from a single unified interface. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (~$1.25-1.36M raised), the company was acquired by Jive Software in 2013, less than a year after its initial funding. StreamOnce is no longer an operating company and publishes no active product, developer portal, or API; the streamonce.com domain now redirects to a domain-sale marketplace. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record surfaced via Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Tara Ai
providers.description: Tara AI (Y Combinator W15, originally Gradberry) was a San Jose-based engineering efficiency platform that used fine-tuned LLMs over source control and project data to measure cycle times, benchmarks, and delivery velocity, integrating with GitHub, GitLab, Jira, and Slack. Backed by Aspect Ventures, Y Combinator, and Slack Fund (~$13M raised). As of July 2026 the company is listed as permanently closed on Crunchbase and tara.ai is a parked domain; no public API, developer docs, or SDKs were ever published, and the TARAAI GitHub org has no public repositories.

providers.name: Teamnote
providers.description: TeamNote is an enterprise mobile productivity and secure communication platform founded in Hong Kong in 2014 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2015 batch. Positioned as "Slack for mobile workforces," it gives corporations a mobile-first workspace for team messaging, collaboration, workflow forms, announcements, and content distribution to frontline and deskless staff, with enterprise security and administration controls. The product originally shipped at teamnoteapp.com (its first customer was Cheung Kong Holdings) and the company now presents at teamnote.ai. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documentation surface was discoverable during enrichment; both web properties are bot-protected.

providers.name: TimeBlocks
providers.description: TimeBlocks is a consumer calendar and personal scheduling mobile app developed by Day2Life Inc., a South Korean company backed by 500 Global. Marketed as Korea's #1 decoration calendar, it brings calendar, to-do, memo, and habit tracking together in a single view, with patented drag-and-drop time-block scheduling (US Patent 10,409,474 B2), roughly 1,000 customization items (themes, stickers, fonts), shared and group calendars with real-time notifications, seven home-screen widgets, and cloud sync across devices. It is a native iOS and Android app; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Tomfoolery
providers.description: Tomfoolery, Inc. was a San Francisco mobile-app lab founded in 2012 by Sol Lipman (Chief Product Officer) and Kakul Srivastava (CEO), a team of ex-Yahoo and ex-AOL executives building consumer-grade, mobile-first collaboration apps for the enterprise. Its debut product was Anchor, a real-time conversation platform meant to be a central hub for work discussions, followed by an app called Action. The company raised roughly $1.7M (investors included Andreessen Horowitz) before being acquired by Yahoo in January 2014, after which the Anchor app was shut down. Tomfoolery is now a defunct/deadpooled company with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface. It was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirms there is no API to profile.

providers.name: Wikidocs
providers.description: Wikidocs was a real-time collaboration startup (wikidocs.io) that built a framework for turning any web page into a live, editable, multi-user "docs" service — enabling real-time content creation, editing, and sharing directly in the browser without waiting for updated versions. Backed by Speedinvest, the company was acquired by Atlassian in September 2014 and its collaboration technology was folded into Atlassian's products. Wikidocs no longer operates as an independent product: its former domain, wikidocs.io, is now a parked and email-forwarded registrar domain with no live developer portal, API, documentation, or machine-readable surface to enrich.

providers.name: WorkLife
providers.description: Worklife (Heroik Labs, Inc. d/b/a Worklife) was a San Francisco meeting-productivity application that helped teams run highly effective meetings — agenda generation and tracking, meeting organization, calendaring, collaborative real-time notes, and clear action items — with a Slack integration and free and paid tiers. A 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company, it was acquired by Cisco on October 17, 2016 and folded into the Cisco Spark collaboration platform (worklife.com redirected to notes.ciscospark.com by early 2017). The standalone worklife.com domain no longer resolves and no public API surface was ever published; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Woven Software
providers.description: Woven Software, Inc. (Woven, woven.com) was a Mountain View, California startup that built an AI-powered calendar and scheduling application for professionals, raising roughly $4.8M from investors including Battery Ventures, Felicis, Amplify Partners, Salesforce Ventures, and the Slack Fund. Slack acquired the Woven team in an acqui-hire announced in April 2021 and the Woven calendar product was shut down; the company no longer operates and publishes no APIs, developer portal, or other public API artifacts. The woven.com domain no longer serves the product (HTTPS fails; registration is behind a privacy service). This profile records the company as an exited Battery Ventures portfolio investment with no remaining API surface.

providers.name: SDLC
providers.description: Software Development Life Cycle - A systematic process for planning, creating, testing, and deploying software systems. Effective use of this practice reduces bugs in production and supports a culture of quality-driven development.

providers.name: Gantt Charts
providers.description: Gantt charts are a project-management visualization that depicts tasks, timelines, dependencies, and progress against a calendar. This repository tracks APIs, libraries, and SaaS providers that produce, render, or expose Gantt-chart data for project planning and scheduling use cases.

providers.name: Qube Horizon
providers.description: Qube Horizon is a platform described as offering project management, resource allocation, and analytics services. No public website or API documentation could be verified at the time of this entry, so no APIs are listed below.

providers.name: Outils De Travail Digitaux
providers.description: Outils de Travail Digitaux refers to digital workplace tools and collaboration platforms used in French-speaking business environments.

providers.name: Outils Digitaux
providers.description: Outils Digitaux refers to digital tools and resources for developers, designers, and digital professionals in French-speaking environments.

providers.name: Kwest
providers.description: Kwest was a Berlin-based B2B SaaS platform for the operations behind renewable-energy installations. Founded by Robin Dechant, Marco Holst and Constantin Ehren, it gave solar, heat-pump and smart-meter installers a workflow platform covering project management, inspection documentation, automated report creation and incident management, plus integrations that synced installation data with the CRM, ERP and field-service tools those companies already ran (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Dynamics 365, Odoo, Xentral, weclapp, Zoho, Aurora Solar, Solytic, Praxedo, Zapier and others). Speedinvest invested in 2021. In 2024 Kwest was acquired by Kraken Technologies, the technology arm of Octopus Energy Group, which folded the Kwest workflow platform into the Kraken stack and opened its first development hub in Berlin around the seven-person team. Kwest published no public API or developer program, and the company no longer operates independently - its former getkwest.com domain has lapsed and now serves unrelated third-party content, so it is recorded here as historical only and is not linked as a live website.

providers.name: Blinkist
providers.description: Blinkist is a Berlin-founded subscription learning app that condenses the key ideas of thousands of nonfiction books and podcasts into roughly 15-minute text and audio summaries called "Blinks." Launched in 2012, it is used by millions of readers to learn on the go across categories such as productivity, business, psychology, personal growth, and science, and it also offers Blinkist for Business for teams and organizations. The consumer product is delivered through the web and iOS/Android apps backed by a private mobile backend at api.blinkist.com; Blinkist does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. Blinkist was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by Insight Partners) and enriched with the provider signals that could be verified from its public surface.

providers.name: Cardmunch
providers.description: CardMunch was a mobile business-card scanning service that used human transcription to turn photographed business cards into contact records on iOS. Founded as a Y Combinator and 500 Global backed startup, it was acquired by LinkedIn in January 2011 for a reported sum under $3 million and operated as a free LinkedIn-branded iPhone app. LinkedIn discontinued the app on July 11, 2014, migrating its users to Evernote's business-card scanning feature. CardMunch never published a public developer program, API, or SDK, and the cardmunch.com domain was re-registered by an unrelated party in April 2016 and now hosts an affiliate content blog. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.
